title: Loan Application Underwriting Agent
problem: Manual loan underwriting takes 3–7 business days per application. Loan officers spend 60% of their time gathering and verifying documents — pay stubs, bank statements, tax returns, ID — before they can even begin credit analysis. This delays decisions, frustrates applicants, and loses business to fintechs offering same-day approvals.
solution: An orchestrator agent triggers on a completed loan application submission. It fans out to extract structured data from uploaded documents, calls the credit bureau API, computes debt-to-income ratio, flags risk factors, and produces a pre-filled credit memo. Low-risk applications below configured thresholds are auto-approved. All others route to an underwriter for HITL review with the full credit memo and evidence pack pre-loaded.
whoItsFor: Loan Officers, Credit Underwriters, Retail Banking Operations, Mortgage Processing Teams
workflowSteps: Trigger: completed loan application event fires (web form submission, mobile app, or broker portal API)
DocumentAgent extracts structured data from uploaded files — income (pay stubs, employer letters), assets (bank statements, investment accounts), identity (government ID, address proof)
CreditAgent calls credit bureau API (Experian, Equifax, TransUnion); retrieves credit score, payment history, open accounts, and derogatory marks
RiskAgent computes: debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio (secured), employment stability score, and risk tier (A/B/C/D)
PolicyAgent retrieves current lending policy from RAG index — checks product eligibility, rate band, maximum LTV for product type
Orchestrator assembles credit memo: applicant summary, income/asset verification results, credit profile, risk tier, policy match, and preliminary rate recommendation
Decision gate: if risk score < auto-approval threshold AND all hard rules pass → issue conditional approval letter automatically
Otherwise: route credit memo + full evidence pack to underwriter HITL queue with 48h SLA alert
Underwriter reviews memo, may request additional docs (agent sends request to applicant), and issues final decision
On approval: agent drafts offer letter, triggers downstream loan origination system
keyInsights: The power is in the document extraction layer — most underwriting delay is document-chasing, not credit analysis. By parallelising extraction (income, assets, ID) and running the credit bureau call concurrently, the agent compresses 2–3 hours of manual data gathering into under 3 minutes. The HITL gate preserves regulatory compliance (underwriter accountability) while eliminating low-value labour. Auto-approval is only safe when hard rules are enforced deterministically — never rely on the LLM for the approval decision itself.

architectureNotes: Three parallel subagents (DocumentAgent, CreditAgent, PolicyAgent) run concurrently after trigger. RiskAgent runs after all three complete, consuming their typed outputs. The credit memo is generated from structured fields only — no free-text hallucination risk in the financial figures. The auto-approval gate uses deterministic rule evaluation (not LLM output) against configurable thresholds stored in the policy index. All decisions are logged with the full evidence pack for regulatory audit.

tools: Azure AI Document Intelligence (pre-built invoice/ID models)
lending policy docs in PDF/Word indexed monthly

failureModes.mode: Credit bureau API unavailable — application stalls
failureModes.mitigation: Implement fallback to cached credit file (< 30 days old) with staleness flag on the credit memo. If no cache exists, queue for retry and notify applicant of delay.

Set confidence threshold per field type. Low-confidence fields are flagged on the credit memo and routed to the underwriter queue regardless of risk score — never auto-approve with unverified income figures.

failureModes.mode: Auto-approval threshold misconfigured — higher risk than intended
failureModes.mitigation: Separate approval thresholds from agent code — store in policy index, require dual approval to update, and log every threshold change. Monthly back-test approved cohort against default rates.

failureModes.mode: Adverse action notice not generated for declined applications
failureModes.mitigation: Decline path always triggers adverse action notice generation (ECOA / FCRA requirement). This is a mandatory step in the workflow, not optional. Test coverage must include decline path end-to-end.

scalingConsiderations: Parallel document extraction reduces per-application latency from 20–40 min (manual) to under 3 minutes regardless of document count.
Credit bureau APIs typically cost $0.50–$2.00 per pull; batch applications overnight where same-day decision is not required to manage cost.
Auto-approval rate depends on product mix; target 40–60% for prime personal loans, lower for mortgages. Monitor auto-approval rate monthly — a sudden spike may indicate threshold drift.
Underwriter HITL queue should never exceed 48 hours; add SLA alerting and dynamic queue routing if backlog grows.
Document extraction models degrade on unusual document formats (hand-written forms, non-standard payslips from international employers) — maintain a human review queue for extraction failures.

integrations.note: Application form data and uploaded document files
